title_en: Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper Office v. Guangxi Coal Mine Workers' Newspaper Office — dispute over the right to use TV program schedules
keywords_en: civil; copyright dispute; right-to-use dispute; second instance; intermediate people's court; Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region; legal person; Copyright Law; General Principles of the Civil Law; whether TV program schedules constitute news of current events; ownership of the right to use TV program schedules; whether the act of reprinting constitutes infringement; reversal; reprinting of TV program schedules; ruling of the Copyright Bureau; counterclaim for defamation; copyright; dispute over right to use TV program schedules
full_text_en:
Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper Office v. Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office — dispute over right to use TV program schedules

Plaintiff: Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper Office.
Legal Representative: Liu Qinghong, Editor-in-Chief and Director of the newspaper.
Agent ad litem: Liu Guikuan, lawyer of Guangxi First Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Fu Xiaorong, Deputy Editor-in-Chief of Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper Office.

Defendant: Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office.
Legal Representative: Liu Feng, Editor-in-Chief of the newspaper.
Agent ad litem: Meng Qinguo, Professor of Law School of Guangxi University.
Agent ad litem: Qin Baichang, Deputy Director of Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office.

The plaintiff, Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper Office, filed a lawsuit with the Heshan City People's Court of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region against the defendant, Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office, over a dispute concerning the right to use TV program schedules.

The plaintiff, Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper Office, alleged: Since its founding in 1979, with the consent of the Autonomous Region Radio and Television Department and China TV Newspaper, the plaintiff obtained the right to publish TV program schedules of Guangxi Television Station and China Central Television (CCTV). China TV Newspaper also authorized the plaintiff to pursue, within Guangxi, infringements by non-radio and television newspapers of the right to publish CCTV program schedules without authorization. The plaintiff successively published statements in the *Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper* prohibiting unauthorized publication of relevant TV program schedules. Other newspapers ceased such publication, but the defendant continued to publish the program schedules of Guangxi Television Station and CCTV in the gutter of its newspaper published every Monday. The defendant's act infringed upon the plaintiff's legitimate rights and interests, affected the distribution of the plaintiff's newspaper within the coal mine system of the Autonomous Region and in Heshan City, and caused the plaintiff substantial economic losses. Therefore, the plaintiff requested the court to order the defendant to immediately cease the infringing act of publishing the one-week TV program schedules of Guangxi Television Station and CCTV, make a public apology, and compensate for economic losses.

The defendant, Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office, argued: TV program schedules are current news. According to the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, current news is not protected by law; neither authors nor publishers enjoy copyright. The defendant's newspaper had indeed been publishing the one-week TV program schedules of Guangxi Television Station and CCTV since 1987, but it had neither reproduced the TV program schedules and articles from the plaintiff's newspaper nor copied and sold the entire *Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper*. Therefore, the plaintiff's claim of infringement was unfounded. The reason the defendant did not comply with the regulations and rulings of the superior copyright authority was that they had no legal basis and were not in the interests of the people. Before the ruling of the Autonomous Region Copyright Bureau became effective, the plaintiff prematurely published news of the defendant being ruled and punished in the *Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper* and on Guangxi Television Station, damaging the defendant's reputation. For this reason, the defendant demanded that the plaintiff make a public apology on the same media and compensate for economic losses of 20,000 yuan.

After public hearing, the Heshan City People's Court found: The plaintiff's *Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper* was approved for publication in December 1979 and distributed within Guangxi. Subsequently, the plaintiff entered into an agreement with China TV Newspaper: China TV Newspaper would provide the plaintiff with CCTV program schedules, which the plaintiff would publish or reprint in its newspaper, paying China TV Newspaper a fee of 80 yuan per issue. Pursuant to Document No. Gui Fa Zi (1987) 35 of the Guangxi Radio and Television Department, the plaintiff orally agreed with Guangxi Television Station that the plaintiff would publish the station's one-week TV program schedules, paying Guangxi Television Station a fee of 100 yuan per issue. Without the plaintiff's consent, the defendant, Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office, starting from 1987, reprinted in its newspaper every Monday the one-week TV program schedules of CCTV and Guangxi Television Station that were published in the plaintiff's newspaper. On February 1, 1988, and May 8, 1989, the plaintiff published statements in its newspaper: Without the permission of this newspaper, no newspaper or periodical may reprint or publish the one-week TV program schedules of this newspaper; violators will be held legally liable. After the Autonomous Region Copyright Bureau issued Document No. Gui Quan Zi (1989) 9, "Notice on the Reprinting of Radio and Television Program Schedules," on September 22, 1989, the defendant continued to reprint the plaintiff's one-week TV program schedules. On February 4, 1990, the plaintiff filed a complaint with the Autonomous Region Copyright Bureau, requesting that the defendant cease infringement, apologize, and compensate for losses. The Autonomous Region Copyright Bureau, upon review, found that the defendant's unauthorized reprinting of the plaintiff's one-week TV program schedules violated relevant regulations and constituted an infringement. On July 24 of the same year, it issued a ruling: the defendant shall immediately cease reprinting the plaintiff's one-week TV program schedules; publish an apology to the plaintiff in the newspaper; and compensate the plaintiff for economic losses of 6,360 yuan. The defendant refused to comply and continued reprinting the plaintiff's one-week TV program schedules. On August 27 of the same year, the plaintiff published the content of the Autonomous Region Copyright Bureau's ruling in its newspaper and on Guangxi Television Station. On August 15, 1991, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the court.

The Heshan City People's Court held that TV program schedules fall within the scope of forecast news and should be regarded as current news. According to Article 5, item (2) of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, no news unit or individual enjoys copyright in current news, and anyone may freely use it. The plaintiff's claim of infringement had no legal basis and was not supported. At the same time, the plaintiff published the ruling of the Autonomous Region Copyright Bureau, which had not yet taken legal effect, in its own newspaper and on Guangxi Television Station, thereby damaging the defendant's reputation. The defendant's counterclaim for an apology had merit and should be supported, but the request for compensation of economic losses of 20,000 yuan lacked basis and was not supported. Accordingly, on December 25, 1991, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. Reject the plaintiff's claims; 2. The plaintiff shall publicly apologize to the defendant in the *Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper*; reject the defendant's counterclaim for compensation of economic losses of 20,000 yuan.

After the first-instance judgment was announced, the plaintiff, Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper Office, appealed to the Liuzhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangxi. The grounds for appeal were: The first-instance judgment erred in treating TV program schedules as current news and not protecting them. The appellant should have the right to use the radio and television program schedules. The appellee, Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office, insulted and vilified the appellant in court and subsequently further disseminated such conduct through its newspaper, infringing the appellant's right to reputation. The appellant requested the court to reverse the original judgment, order the appellee to cease infringement, and compensate for economic losses. The appellee, Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office, agreed with the first-instance judgment and filed a counterclaim regarding the appellant's claim of reputation infringement.

The Liuzhou Intermediate People's Court, upon trial, held: Current news refers to reports by news organizations such as newspapers, news agencies, radio stations, and television stations on recent domestic and international political events or social events. A one-week TV program schedule is a forecast by the television station to inform viewers in advance of the programs for the week so that they can choose to watch them at the scheduled times. Therefore, a TV program schedule does not fall within the scope of current news as referred to in Article 5, item (2) of the Copyright Law. The Notice of the State Press and Publication Administration dated March 30, 1988, "Notice on the Reprinting of Radio and Television Program Schedules," provides: "Newspapers and periodicals in newspaper form may reprint the radio and television program schedules for the current day and the following day as published in the radio and television newspaper. However, they may not reprint or excerpt the radio and television program schedules for one week (or more than one week) at one time. If reprinting the entire week's radio and television program schedules is necessary, consultation with the relevant radio and television newspaper office shall be conducted." The appellee, without the permission of the appellant, reprinted the one-week TV program schedules, violating the provisions of the said notice. The appellant, through an agreement with the television station, obtained for value the right to disseminate the one-week TV program schedules to the public in newspaper form within Guangxi, which is protected by law. The appellee's conduct constituted an intentional infringement of the appellant's civil rights and interests. Pursuant to Article 106, paragraph 2, of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the appellee shall bear civil liability.

The appellant's appeal had merit and should be supported; the first-instance judgment was indeed improper and should be corrected. As for the appellant's claim at the second instance that the appellee infringed its right to reputation and the appellee's counterclaim in this regard, these were newly added independent claims, pertaining to a different legal relationship, and should not be tried together with the principal claim. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment on November 25, 1994:

1. Affirm the part of item (2) of the civil judgment (1991) He Fa Min Pan Zi No. 46 of the Heshan City People's Court that rejected the defendant's counterclaim for compensation of economic losses of 20,000 yuan.

2. Reverse item (1) and the part of item (2) of the said judgment concerning the plaintiff's public apology to the defendant in the *Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper*.

3. The appellee, Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office, shall immediately cease the infringing act of publishing the one-week TV program schedules of the *Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper* in its newspaper.

4. The appellee, Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office, shall pay the appellant, Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper Office, compensation for economic losses of 50,000 yuan, payable within ten days after this judgment takes effect.

5. The appellee, Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office, shall publicly apologize to the appellant, Guangxi Radio and Television Newspaper Office, in its newspaper. The content of the apology shall be subject to review by the court.

The first-instance case acceptance fee and counterclaim fee totaling 1,220 yuan, and the second-instance case acceptance fee of 2,010 yuan, totaling 3,230 yuan, shall be borne by the appellee, Guangxi Coal Miner Newspaper Office.
